input.prompt: Painted front cover illustration in the tradition of 1960s American humour magazines: thick gouache and watercolour over a lively, confident pen-and-ink drawing, wildly exaggerated caricature proportions (huge heads, small bodies, big hands and feet), comic body language, warm saturated colours, visible brush strokes and paper grain. Scene: the roof of an old 1960s Wall Street skyscraper. In the middle ground a rooftop swimming pool filled to the brim with heaps of shiny gold coins that glint. On the right a ridiculously tall, spindly diving ladder rises to a long springy diving board that sticks out high over the pool; the end of the board is EMPTY and bends a little. In the foreground, large in the bottom half of the picture, four caricatured men stand in a row seen FROM BEHIND, heads thrown back, staring up at the empty board, their faces hidden: from left, a man with an enormous mop of dark curly hair in a long rust-red overcoat, a notebook with coloured tabs tucked under his arm; a slim man in a sharp black suit with his hands in his pockets; a broad-shouldered man in a black leather jacket pointing up at the board; a young man with shaggy black hair in a navy-blue flight suit shading his eyes, a white pilot helmet under his arm. Other old towers and water tanks around. The top quarter of the picture is open painted cerulean sky with a few soft clouds and nothing else, left clear for a masthead. No flags, no patches. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no signs with writing.

Editorial cartoon in the tradition of 1960s American newspaper and humour-magazine cartoons: pen-and-ink with crosshatching and loose watercolour wash. A deep swimming pool brim-full of gold coins, seen in three-quarter view, its near wall cut away like a diagram so we see the coins inside down to the floor. Top left: a giant brass faucet pours a thick stream of gold coins into the pool. Upper right: a long diving board juts out over the pool, nobody on it. Middle left: coins spill over a little spout in the pool's rim into a wooden bucket standing on the ground. Bottom: inside the cutaway, a huge round drain plug on a heavy chain sits in the pool floor. FOUR LARGE blank cream cardboard luggage tags hang on strings, each tag wide and horizontal and about a quarter of the picture's width, clearly separated and not overlapping anything important: one from the faucet, one from the tip of the diving board, one from the bucket's handle, one from the drain plug's chain. Every tag completely blank and evenly lit. Background: a deep blue-black ink-wash night sky with dry-brush texture. No people. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no signs with writing.

Editorial cartoon in the tradition of 1960s American newspaper and humour-magazine cartoons: pen-and-ink with crosshatching and loose watercolour wash. An old brass balance scale standing in the middle, its beam perfectly level. On the left pan sits a black graduation mortarboard cap with a tassel; on the right pan sits a lucky iron horseshoe. Below each pan hangs one LARGE blank cream cardboard luggage tag on a string, each tag wide and horizontal, about a third of the picture's width; one more LARGE wide blank cream tag hangs from the front of the scale's base. Every tag completely blank and evenly lit, not overlapping each other. Background: a deep green watercolour wash filling the whole frame edge to edge, pigment blooms and paper grain. No people. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no signs with writing.
